question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European Factory Headquarters in India]
options: English East India Company – Surat (First Factory, 1608)
Dutch East India Company – Pulicat (First Factory on Coromandel Coast)
French East India Company – Calicut (First French Factory in India)
wrong_fact: The first French factory in India was established at Surat (1668), not Calicut. Pondicherry became the principal French settlement later.
explanation: The English established their first factory at Surat in 1608 under Thomas Best's victory. The Portuguese made Goa their headquarters after capturing it in 1510. The Dutch set up their first factory at Masulipatnam (1605) on the Coromandel Coast, and later Pulicat became a major Dutch centre. The French opened their first factory at Surat in 1668 under Colbert's initiative, not Calicut.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Factory Administration – Subordinate Factories / Presidencies]
options: Fort St. George (Madras) – Seat of Madras Presidency
Fort William (Calcutta) – Seat of Bengal Presidency
Bombay Castle – Seat of Bombay Presidency
Fort St. David (Cuddalore) – Seat of Madras Presidency superseding Fort St. George
wrong_fact: Fort St. David at Cuddalore was a subordinate settlement under the Madras Presidency; it never superseded Fort St. George as the presidency seat. Fort St. George remained the seat throughout.
explanation: The three English Presidencies were centred at Fort St. George (Madras, 1644), Fort William (Calcutta, 1700), and Bombay Castle. Fort St. David at Cuddalore served as a refuge when Madras was captured by the French (1746) but was always subordinate to Madras and never became the presidency headquarters permanently.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Factory Administration – Factories and their founding dates/regions]
options: Masulipatnam – First English factory on Coromandel Coast (1611)
Hooghly – Portuguese factory established before English presence in Bengal
Armagaon – Dutch principal factory on Coromandel Coast before Pulicat became dominant
Balasore – English factory in Orissa serving as entry point to Bengal trade
wrong_fact: Armagaon was an English factory (established 1626), not a Dutch factory. Pulicat was the Dutch principal factory on the Coromandel Coast, established in 1610. The Dutch never held Armagaon.
explanation: Masulipatnam (1611) was indeed the first English factory on the Coromandel Coast. The Portuguese established themselves at Hooghly in 1537, predating English presence in Bengal. Balasore in Orissa functioned as the English entry point to Bengal trade before Calcutta. However, Armagaon was an English fort and factory (1626), not Dutch. The Dutch principal factory on the Coromandel Coast was Pulicat (1610).
